conservation.notes: Hunted for its plumage in the late 19th century, since recovered.

human_tolerance.notes: Forages in flight and by picking up objects while swimming, walking or wading; breeds on flat factory roofs as well as on the ground, and scavenges refuse and fish waste, so it is at home on a built-up shore.

phases.name: nesting
phases.note: Ground colonies on islands and lake shores, and increasingly on flat factory roofs. The bird takes three years to reach breeding plumage, starting from largely brown juvenile plumage that changes with each autumn moult.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: After breeding, birds gather in large flocks on the Great Lakes and along the coasts, feeding on refuse and on winter-killed fish.

vocalizations.description: A repeated nasal, laughing 'kee-yer' given by competing birds; the cited recording is exactly this, a squabble between gulls over winter-killed fish on lake ice.

A single sharp descending cry, given by an adult when a chick or a nest is threatened and by birds disputing a food source; the duration band is authored and no second openly licensed recording is cited.

conservation.note: IUCN category from Wikidata P141; the plumage-hunting history from the article's status section.

range.note: Country list derived from the article's breeding and wintering range across North America, with Greenland recorded for the Greenland population.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: 'forage in flight or pick up objects while swimming, walking or wading'.

traits.nest_type.note: 'They nest colonially on the ground, often on islands, but also increasingly on flat factory roofs.'

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of 'Adults weigh from 300 to 700 grams'.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of 'an average length of 43 to 54 centimetres'.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Midpoint of 'a wingspan that ranges from 105 to 117 centimetres'.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'The average lifespan of an individual that reaches adulthood is 10.9 years'; the same paragraph records the oldest known bird as 28 years, alive in Cleveland, Ohio in 2021.

traits.diet.note: Wikipedia: 'They are omnivorous; their diet may include insects, fish, grain, eggs, earthworms and rodents.' 0.35/0.25/0.20/0.20 is a judgement that keeps insects and earthworms in `invertebrate`, grain in `seed`, and fish, eggs and rodents in `vertebrate` and `fish`.

traits.social.note: Colonial ground nesters that are 'faithful to its nesting site, if not its mate, from year to year'.

traits.activity_pattern.note: The article describes foraging in flight, by swimming, walking and wading without restricting it to daylight, and the winter flocking it records is around-the-clock; Cathemeral is a judgement.

traits.defense.note: Authored: the bird flies off rather than defending a food item, though it will squabble at one.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement, based on a bird that scavenges refuse and nests on flat factory roofs and so tolerates people closely.

habitat.use.note: Foraging in flight, on the water surface, on the shore and on flat roofs from the diet and nesting sentences; authored split.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Roosts on roofs, jetties, water and low perches rather than in tree canopy.

habitat.resources.note: The omnivorous diet list from Wikipedia, plus ground nest sites and loafing perches. The schema's tag set has no `fish` tag, so fish and eggs are carried by `small_vertebrate`. `carrion` is declared because fsm-seabird-predator-v1 scavenges on it, and winter-killed fish on the ice are exactly that.

habitat.requires.note: Every habitat statement in the article starts from water or from refuse near people; 2 km is an authored radius.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Nesting on flat factory roofs and picking up refuse from the foraging and nesting sentences; the numeric tolerances are authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: The article describes a discrete breeding season on the ground followed by large flocks elsewhere, which is PartialMigration rather than outright migration, because a share overwinters on the Great Lakes.

seasonal.winter_fraction.note: Judgement, 0.6: the article records a large wintering flock on the Great Lakes but gives no share of the world population overwintering there.

seasonal.phases.note: Ground colonial nesting and the post-breeding flocks from Wikipedia; the month-day boundaries are judgements.

seasonal.life_stages.note: 'This gull takes three years to reach its breeding plumage starting with the largely brown juvenile plumage, its appearance changing with each fall moult'; duration_days is 1095 and scale 0.85 is a judgement for the brown juvenile plumage.

vocalizations.squabble.note: The xeno-canto record's own remarks are 'Squabbling over winter-killed fish on the lake ice', which is what the description describes. The duration band is authored.

vocalizations.alarm_call.note: Authored. The Wikipedia article does not describe the call, and no second openly licensed recording is cited, so the description and duration are the field's own judgement.

look.note: White head and body, pale grey back, black outer primaries with white spots, and a yellow bill ringed in black - the ring that names the bird, drawn as an extra part on the bill. The proportions are authored from the article's 43-54 cm length and 105-117 cm wingspan.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared territorial-predator program, which matches how a gull works: patrol by flight, take live prey, scavenge carrion, drink, retreat from a threat. flee_m is kept low at 30 m because the species is a bold opportunist around people.
